A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new 3D reconstruction framework, which is able to reconstruct surfaces with a high level of accuracy and robustness.

we have proposed three new methods that are the first to use ‘true' isometric constraints, the first to handle noise in the template and the input image, and that are more accurate than the state of the art.

our convex pointwise method provides a fast initialization and our convex continuous surface method and nonconvex continuous surface method provide a fast and accurate refinement of the initialization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the convex approximations to isometry are very useful to initialize a nonconvex method that uses the ‘true isometric’ constraints.
the convex inextensible constraint is a good approximation to the true isometric constraint.
the use of convex approximations for isometry is not always a bad idea.
